text:
jules_pm: Quick thread: we need a compact invite rubric for design partners that prioritizes impact & low onboarding cost. Want something the intake team can use without back-and-forth.

alex_cs: Proposal: 1) Must show at least one concrete success metric, 2) Must commit an owner for weekly check-ins, 3) Provide a PoC or call Redwood API once during triage.

nora_eng: Add lightweight engineering checks: successful auth + a simple request/response sample, and a stated expected p95 latency. If they need private infra, route out.

kai_research: We'll ask for 6 representative prompts (edge cases included) so we can map the partner to our eval buckets quickly. We'll run a short 6-prompt battery during triage.

peter_ops: Ops constraint: initial cohort limit 6 seats. Require a data handling acknowledgement in intake (logs retention + contact for compliance). Also capture preferred timezone window.

jules_pm: Good. Let's define the scoring: Integration readiness (0-6), Impact (0-6), Owner bandwidth (0-4), Compliance blockers (0-4). Sort by total. Auto-reject if Integration readiness=0.

alex_cs: Signals to track in beta: daily API calls, p95 latency, bug count (priority >=P2), weekly partner responsiveness score (1-5). Keep it short.

nora_eng: For onboarding checklist: API key issued, rate limits set, model pinned (if requested), monitoring webhook configured, and a smoke test done by partner.

kai_research: I'll draft the 6 prompts and a 1-page report template.

peter_ops: I'll make the intake field list and data checkbox. Seats claimed via the intake tracker.

jules_pm: Owners: kai -> evals, nora -> eng checklist, alex -> CS template + triage guide, peter -> ops gating. Can we have drafts by tomorrow 9am?

oncall-bot: reminder: onboarding capacity this sprint: 6 seats.

jules_pm: Thanks. Final note: Public partner note (3 bullets): 1) Typical timeline (2-4 weeks), 2) What we expect (PoC, weekly syncs, sample prompts), 3) What we provide (seat, eval report, engineering triage). Keep wording tight.
